Crescent Moon Pose Quad Stretch

Stretching - Mobility Revised

PurposeStretches the front of the hip and thigh of the back leg at once, which is a pair that often tightens from a lot of sitting and can limit how far the hip extends when you walk or run.

  1. Kneel on one knee with the other foot forward, both bent to about ninety degrees
  2. Squeeze the glute of the kneeling leg to push that hip forward
  3. Raise both arms overhead and lengthen through your side
  4. Keep your ribs down so the stretch stays in the hip, not the lower back
  5. Hold for thirty seconds, then change sides
ea_crescent_moon_pose_quad_stretch

Crescent Moon Pose Quad Stretch with Block

Stretching - Mobility

PurposeThe same hip and thigh stretch with a block under the hands, so you can hold the position without needing the balance the full version demands. The version to use while the hip is still tight.

  1. Kneel on one knee with the other foot forward and a block beside the front foot
  2. Rest one or both hands on the block to steady yourself
  3. Push the hip of the kneeling leg forward by squeezing that glute
  4. Keep your torso upright and your ribs pulled down
  5. Hold for thirty seconds, then swap legs
ea_crescent_moon_pose_quad_stretch_with_block

Cross Body Elbow Pull Shoulder Stretch

Stretching - Mobility

PurposePulling by the elbow rather than the wrist keeps the pressure off the shoulder joint and puts the stretch where it belongs — across the back of the shoulder, which tightens after pressing and throwing.

  1. Stand tall and bring one arm straight across your chest
  2. Hook the opposite hand behind that elbow, not the forearm
  3. Draw the arm gently across your body until you feel the back of the shoulder stretch
  4. Keep both shoulders down and facing forward — do not rotate the torso
  5. Hold for twenty to thirty seconds, then change arms
ea_cross_body_elbow_pull_shoulder_stretch

Cross Body Shoulder Stretch

Stretching - Mobility

PurposeThe simplest way to open the back of the shoulder, which is the area that closes up after a session of rows and pull-ups. Quick enough to do between sets.

  1. Stand or sit tall with your shoulders level
  2. Reach one arm straight across the front of your chest
  3. Support it with the other forearm and draw it closer to your body
  4. Keep the working shoulder pressed down, away from your ear
  5. Hold for twenty seconds, then do the other side
ea_cross_body_shoulder_stretch

Crossover Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch

Stretching - Mobility No purpose Revised

Purposenot written yet (H3 pending)

  2. Engage your core and rotate your torso towards your right leg, placing both arms straight and pulling on the outside of your right thigh
  3. Gently push your hips forward while keeping your spine neutral to stretch
  4. Hold this position for the desired duration, then switch sides and repeat

Exercise Ball Lying Side Lat Stretch V.2

Stretching - Mobility No purpose

  2. Allow your bottom arm to hang in a comfortable position for support over the ball and extend your left arm overhead, reaching it along the line of your body

Exercise Ball Seated Hamstring Stretch

Exercise Ball Seated Quad Stretch

Extension of Arms in Vertical Stretch

Fixed Bar Stretch

  2. Step back slightly and lean your hips backward, allowing your arms to extend fully and your upper body to lean forward. Keep your spine neutral and your knees bent
  3. Lean backwards and down to the floor while pulling back with your hips to feel a deep stretch in your shoulders, upper back, and lats

Foam Roller Back

Stretching - Mobility Revised

PurposeRolling the upper back can help maintain the extension that sitting tends to reduce, which is what lets you hold a bar overhead or keep the chest up in a squat. Stay above the ribs — never roll the lower back.

  1. Lie on your back with a foam roller across your upper back, below the shoulder blades
  2. Support your head with your hands and lift your hips off the floor
  3. Roll slowly up and down between the shoulder blades and the base of the neck
  4. Pause on any tight spot and breathe for a few seconds
  5. Stop at the bottom of the ribs — do not roll onto the lower back
ea_foam_roller_back upper_back

Foam Roller Calves

Stretching - Mobility

PurposeTight calves limit how far the ankle bends, which shows up as heels lifting in a squat and as a shortened stride when running. Rolling them is faster than stretching at restoring that movement.

  1. Sit on the floor with a foam roller under one calf and the other leg crossed over it
  2. Press your hands into the floor to lift your hips
  3. Roll slowly from just above the ankle to just below the knee
  4. Stop on tight spots and rotate the leg in and out to reach the sides
  5. Spend about a minute per leg, then switch
ea_foam_roller_calves

Foam Roller Lateral Quads

Stretching - Mobility Revised

PurposeThe outside of the thigh gets tight in anyone who runs or cycles, and that tightness pulls on the outside of the knee. This can be one of the more uncomfortable rolling spots — keep the pressure tolerable rather than judging effectiveness by how much it hurts. Mild muscular tension is normal, but sharp, radiating, or joint pain is a signal to stop.

  1. Lie on your side with a foam roller under the outside of one thigh
  2. Support yourself on your forearm and the opposite foot
  3. Roll slowly from just below the hip to just above the knee
  4. Never roll directly over the knee or the hip bone
  5. Pause on the tightest spots and breathe, then change sides
ea_foam_roller_lateral_quads

Foam Roller Quads-

Stretching - Mobility Revised

PurposeRolling the front of the thigh before training helps the knee bend more freely, and after training it helps with the stiffness that follows heavy squatting. One of the few rolling spots that is easy to reach.

  1. Lie face down with a foam roller under the front of both thighs
  2. Support yourself on your forearms with your elbows under your shoulders
  3. Roll slowly from just below the hips to just above the knees
  4. Pause on tender areas and breathe until they ease — mild tension is normal, but stop if you feel sharp, radiating, or joint pain
  5. Roll one leg at a time if you want more pressure
ea_foam_roller_quads

Forearms Pull with Opposite Hand Stretch

Stretching - Mobility Revised

PurposeStretches the forearm flexor and extensor muscles that grip all day, whether on a bar or a keyboard. If you have ongoing elbow pain from overuse, it's worth getting assessed rather than relying on stretching alone.

  1. Extend one arm straight out in front of you at shoulder height, palm down
  2. Use the opposite hand to pull the fingers gently back toward you
  3. Keep the extended elbow straight throughout
  4. Hold, then turn the palm up and pull the fingers down for the other side of the forearm
  5. Hold each position for twenty seconds, then change arms
ea_forearms_pull_with_opposite_hand_stretch

Forearms Stretch on Wall

Stretching - Mobility

PurposeUses the wall so you can stretch both forearms at once and control the intensity with your own bodyweight. Better than the hand-pull version when the forearms are properly tight.

  1. Stand facing a wall and place both palms flat on it at chest height, fingers up
  2. Keep your arms straight and your shoulders down
  3. Step back slightly and press your palms into the wall
  4. Lean away until you feel the stretch along the underside of both forearms
  5. Hold for thirty seconds, breathing steadily
ea_forearms_stretch_on_wall

Forearms Stretch on Wall Fingers Facing Down

Stretching - Mobility Revised

PurposeTurning the fingers down reaches the muscles on the top of the forearm — the side connected to the outer elbow, a common spot for tightness from repetitive gripping.

  1. Face a wall and place both palms on it with the fingers pointing straight down
  2. Keep your arms straight and your elbows soft, not locked hard
  3. Press the palms flat against the wall
  4. Lean in gently until you feel the stretch across the top of the forearms
  5. Hold for twenty to thirty seconds without forcing it
ea_forearms_stretch_on_wall_fingers_facing_down

Front Shoulder Stretch with Bar

Stretching - Mobility No purpose Revised

Purposenot written yet (H3 pending)

  1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a bar with both hands, palms facing down, and hands placed slightly wider than shoulder-width apart
  2. Extend your arms straight down in front of you at shoulder height, keeping your spine neutral and core engaged
  3. Gently raise the bar overhead and bend them both at 90 degrees to lower them until you feel a stretch in your shoulders
  4. Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds. Repeat as needed
ea_front_shoulder_stretch_with_bar

Half Neck Rolls

Stretching - Mobility Revised

PurposeMoves the neck through a controlled range without taking it backwards. Work only in a comfortable, symptom-free range and do not force the end of it. Half rolls are the gentler version and still reach the muscles that tighten from screens and from carrying stress.

  1. Sit or stand tall with your shoulders relaxed and down
  2. Drop your chin toward your chest
  3. Roll your head slowly to one side until your ear moves toward that shoulder
  4. Roll back through the middle to the other side, keeping the chin low the whole time
  5. Never roll the head backwards; continue for the set time
ea_half_neck_rolls neck

Hamstring Lying Curl Up Stretch

  1. Lie on your back with your legs extended and your arms at your sides
  2. Bend your right knee and bring it towards your chest until thigh is vertical to the floor, interlacing your fingers behind your thigh
  3. Slowly straighten your right leg, extending your heel towards the ceiling and feeling the stretch in your hamstring. Keep your left leg extended and flat on the floor

  3. Pull your right leg gently towards your torso, feeling the stretch in your hamstring. Keep your left leg extended and flat on the floor

PurposePressing the palms together and lowering them stretches both forearms and wrists evenly, which matters for anyone doing push-ups, front squats or handstands — all of which need the wrist to bend back.

  2. Keep the palms touching along their whole length
  3. Lower the hands slowly toward your stomach, keeping the elbows out
  4. Stop when you feel the stretch across the wrists and forearms

Lats Stretch Elbow on Wall

  2. Step back and hinge at the hips so your chest drops toward the floor
  3. Let your head sink between your arms and lengthen through the side
  4. Breathe into the side of your ribs, where the stretch should be felt
  5. Hold for thirty seconds, then change sides

Lats Stretch on Wall

Stretching - Mobility

PurposeReaching both hands to a wall and sitting the hips back stretches both lats at once. Quick, needs nothing, and it is the standard thing to do before any overhead lifting.

  1. Stand facing a wall and place both hands on it at about head height
  2. Walk your feet back until your arms are straight
  3. Push your hips back and let your chest sink toward the floor
  4. Keep your arms straight and your head between your upper arms
  5. Hold for thirty seconds, breathing into the sides of your back
ea_lats_stretch_on_wall

Leg Extended Stretch on Bench

Stretching - Mobility No purpose Revised

Purposenot written yet (H3 pending)

  2. Extend your right leg forward until it is parallel to the floor, keeping your leg straight
  3. Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, feeling the stretch in your hamstring and lower back
  4. Slowly bring your right leg back to the starting position with both feet flat on the floor. Repeat the stretch with your left leg extended. Alternate sides for the desired number of repetitions

Legs Hand Reach Spine Stretch

  2. Slowly bend forward at the hips, reaching your hands towards your feet. Keep your legs straight and your toes pointing up
  3. Continue to reach forward, aiming to touch your toes or go as far as your flexibility allows. Allow your head and neck to relax as you stretch
  4. Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, breathing deeply and steadily

Lunging Straight Leg Calf Stretch

Purposenot written yet (H3 pending)

  1. Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart and your arms at your sides
  2. Step your right foot back into a lunge position, keeping your right leg straight and your heel on the floor. Bend your left knee slightly, keeping your left foot flat on the floor
  3. Lean forward slightly, pressing your hips downward and feeling the stretch in your right calf. Hold this position for 15-30 seconds
  4. Return to the starting position and switch legs, stepping your left foot back and repeating the stretch
ea_lunging_straight_leg_calf_stretch ankle

Lying (prone) Abdominal Stretch

Stretching - Mobility No purpose

Purposenot written yet (H3 pending)

  1. Begin by lying face down on the floor with your legs extended straight behind you and your hands placed under your shoulders, palms flat on the floor
  2. Slowly press your hands into the floor to lift your chest upward, extending your spine. Keep your hips and legs relaxed on the floor
  3. Continue to lift your chest until you feel a comfortable stretch in your abdomen and lower back. Hold this position for 15-30 seconds, keeping your elbows slightly bent
  4. Slowly lower your chest back down to the floor and return to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions
ea_lying_prone_abdominal_stretch

Lying Bent Knee Cross Glutes Stretch

Stretching - Mobility Revised

PurposeReaches the deep muscles at the back of the hip, which are hard to reach with broader stretches. Expect a strong stretch rather than pain, and ease off if it turns sharp or you feel numbness or tingling down the leg.

  1. Lie on your back with both knees bent and feet flat
  2. Cross one ankle over the opposite knee to make a figure four
  3. Reach through the gap and hold the back of the supporting thigh
  4. Draw that leg toward your chest until you feel the stretch in the crossed hip
  5. Hold for thirty seconds, keeping your head and shoulders on the floor, then swap
ea_lying_bent_knee_cross_glutes_stretch

Lying Crossover Stretch

Stretching - Mobility No purpose

Purposenot written yet (H3 pending)

  1. Lie on your back with your legs extended straight and your arms out to the sides to form a T shape
  2. Bend and lift your right leg and cross it over your body, aiming to touch the floor on the left side, and extend your left arm to hold your right knee down
  3. Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, feeling the stretch in your lower back and hips
  4. Slowly return your right leg to the starting position. Repeat the stretch with your left leg, crossing it over your body to the right side. Alternate sides for the desired number of repetitions
ea_lying_crossover_stretch lower_back

Lying Face Down Quadriceps Stretch

Stretching - Mobility

PurposeStretches the front of the thigh with the hip flat on the floor, which stops you cheating by arching your back. That makes it a truer stretch than the standing version most people do.

  1. Lie face down with your forehead resting on your free arm
  2. Bend one knee and reach back to hold that ankle or foot
  3. Draw the heel toward your backside, keeping the hip pressed into the floor
  4. Stop as soon as you feel the front of the thigh stretch, not the knee
  5. Hold for thirty seconds, then change legs
ea_lying_face_down_quadriceps_stretch

Lying Glute Stretch

Stretching - Mobility No purpose

Purposenot written yet (H3 pending)

  1. Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor
  2. Cross your right ankle over your left knee, forming a figure-four position
  3. Grasp the back of your left thigh with both hands and gently pull your left leg towards your chest. Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, feeling the stretch in your right glute and hip
  4. Slowly release your left leg and return to the starting position. Repeat the stretch with your left ankle crossed over your right knee. Alternate sides for the desired number of repetitions
ea_lying_glute_stretch

Lying Hip Flexor Stretch

Stretching - Mobility No purpose

Purposenot written yet (H3 pending)

  1. Lie on your back with your legs straight on the floor
  2. Lift your right knee towards your chest, holding it with both hands to keep it close while extending your left leg straight off floor, keeping it in line with your right foot
  3. Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, then slowly release your right knee and return to the starting position. Repeat the stretch with your left knee lifted towards your chest and your right leg extended. Alternate sides for the desired number of repetitions

Lying Knee Hugs Lower Back Stretch

Stretching - Mobility Revised

PurposeRounds the lower back gently while fully supported on the floor, moving the lumbar spine and hips through a comfortable range. Many people find it a pleasant way to ease stiffness after sitting, lifting or standing.

  1. Lie on your back with your legs straight
  2. Draw both knees toward your chest and wrap your arms around them
  3. Pull them in gently until your lower back rounds against the floor
  4. Keep your head and shoulders relaxed on the ground
  5. Hold for thirty seconds, breathing into the lower back
ea_lying_knee_hugs_lower_back_stretch

Lying Knee Pull Glutes Stretch

Stretching - Mobility

PurposePulling one knee across the body reaches the outside of the hip, which is where tightness builds in runners and in anyone who sits with their legs crossed. Gentler than the figure-four version.

  1. Lie on your back with your legs straight and arms out to the sides
  2. Bend one knee and draw it up toward your chest
  3. Use the opposite hand to guide that knee across your body toward the floor
  4. Keep both shoulders flat on the ground as the knee crosses over
  5. Hold for thirty seconds, then bring it back and change legs
ea_lying_knee_pull_glutes_stretch

Lying Knees to Floor Lower Back Stretch

Stretching - Mobility Revised

PurposeA gentle rotation of the spine that opens the lower back and the front of the chest at the same time. A supported way to restore rotation, which the back tends to lose faster than other directions of movement.

  1. Lie on your back with your knees bent and your arms out wide
  2. Keep your knees together and your feet on the floor
  3. Let both knees fall slowly to one side toward the ground
  4. Turn your head the opposite way and keep both shoulders on the floor
  5. Hold for thirty seconds, then bring the knees through the middle to the other side
ea_lying_knees_to_floor_lower_back_stretch

Lying Quadriceps Stretch

Stretching - Mobility No purpose

Purposenot written yet (H3 pending)

  1. Lie face down on the floor with your legs extended straight and your arms resting by your sides
  2. Bend your right knee and reach back with your right hand to grasp your right ankle or foot
  3. Gently pull your right foot towards your glutes, feeling the stretch in your right quadriceps. Keep your hips pressed into the floor
  4. Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, then slowly release your right foot and return to the starting position. Repeat the stretch on your left leg. Alternate sides for the desired number of repetitions
ea_lying_quadriceps_stretch

Lying Side Quadriceps Stretch

Stretching - Mobility No purpose

Purposenot written yet (H3 pending)

  1. Lie on your side with your legs extended straight and your head resting on your lower hand. Extend your top arm and reach back to grasp your top ankle or foot
  2. Bend your top knee and gently pull your foot towards your glutes with your hand, feeling the stretch in your quadriceps. Keep your hips stacked and your body in a straight line
  3. Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, breathing deeply and steadily

Stretching - Mobility

PurposeThe wall holds the leg for you, so the hamstring can relax into the stretch instead of working to hold the position. That makes it far more effective than reaching for your toes while standing.

  2. Raise one leg and rest it flat against the wall, keeping it as straight as you can
  3. Let the other leg lie flat along the floor
  4. Slide your hips closer to the wall to increase the stretch
  5. Hold for thirty to sixty seconds, then change legs

  2. Slowly rotate your torso to the right, keeping your hips facing forward. Twist as far as is comfortable, feeling the stretch in your middle back

  2. Bend your right knee and lower into a side lunge while simultaneously rotating your torso to the right and bringing your left hand to touch your right leg. Keeping your left leg straight
  3. Push off your right foot to return to the starting wide stance position, straightening your right leg and rotating your torso back to the center

  2. Rest the same-side forearm on the straight leg
  3. Reach the opposite arm overhead and over toward that foot
  4. Turn your chest slightly upward rather than folding forward
  5. Hold for thirty seconds, breathing into the top ribs, then switch sides

Runner Stretch

  1. Begin in a standing position with your feet hip-width apart
  2. Step your right foot slightly forward, keeping it straight. Lightly bend your left knee
  3. Lower your torso and arms towards your right foot, reaching down with your hands while keeping your spine neutral

Seated Calf Stretch

Stretching - Mobility No purpose Revised

Purposenot written yet (H3 pending)

Seated Figure Four with Twist Glute Stretch

Stretching - Mobility

PurposeAdding a twist to the figure four reaches deeper into the back of the hip and stretches the lower back at the same time. Can be done in a chair, which makes it practical during a working day.

  1. Sit tall on the floor or a chair and cross one ankle over the opposite knee
  2. Let the crossed knee fall open to the side
  3. Place the opposite hand on that knee and the other hand behind you
  4. Turn your chest toward the crossed leg, lengthening as you go
  5. Hold for thirty seconds, then unwind slowly and change sides

Seated Single Leg Hamstring Stretch

Purposenot written yet (H3 pending)

  2. Bend your left knee and place the sole of your left foot against your right inner thigh. Keep your right leg extended and straight
  3. Reach forward with both hands towards your right foot, keeping your spine neutral. Aim to grasp your toes or reach as far as comfortable

Seated Single Leg Toe Touch Hamstring Stretch

Stretching - Mobility

PurposeOne leg at a time lets you work on the tighter side without the looser one hiding it. Hamstring tightness is almost always uneven, and a two-leg stretch never shows you that.

  1. Sit on the floor with one leg straight out and the other bent, foot to the inner thigh
  2. Sit up tall and turn your chest toward the straight leg
  3. Hinge forward from the hips, not by rounding your back
  4. Reach toward the foot of the straight leg until you feel the stretch behind the thigh
  5. Hold for thirty seconds, then change legs

Seated Straight Leg Calf Stretch

Stretching - Mobility No purpose

Purposenot written yet (H3 pending)

  1. Sit on the floor with your legs extended straight in front of you
  2. Lightly bend both knees and extend your right foot, reaching forward to grasp your toes with your right hand
  3. Gently pull your toes towards you, feeling the stretch in your calf muscle
  4. Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, then slowly release. Repeat on the left leg
ea_seated_straight_leg_calf_stretch ankle

Seated Toe Touch Hamstrings Stretch

Stretching - Mobility Revised

PurposeOne of the most familiar hamstring stretches there is. Done from the hips with a neutral spine it lengthens the hamstrings; done by rounding the back it mostly stretches the spine instead, which is not the point.

  1. Sit on the floor with both legs straight out in front of you
  2. Sit up tall and lengthen through the top of your head
  3. Hinge forward from the hips, keeping your back as flat as you can
  4. Reach toward your feet and stop where the stretch is felt behind the thighs
  5. Hold for thirty seconds, breathing out as you settle deeper

Side Bend Standing Lats Stretch

Stretching - Mobility

PurposeOpens the whole side of the body from the hip to the hand, including the lats and the muscles between the ribs. Takes ten seconds and needs no equipment, which makes it easy to do often.

  1. Stand tall with your feet hip width apart
  2. Reach one arm straight overhead and hold the wrist with the other hand
  3. Lengthen upward first, then bend to the opposite side
  4. Keep both feet flat and your hips facing forward
  5. Hold for twenty seconds, then come back up and do the other side

Stretching - Mobility

PurposeOpens one side of the chest at a time, which lets you spend longer on the tighter side. Chest tightness is often asymmetric, especially in people who work at a desk with a mouse.

  1. Stand beside a wall and place one palm flat on it behind you at shoulder height
  2. Keep that arm straight and the shoulder pressed down
  3. Turn your body slowly away from the wall
  4. Stop when you feel the stretch across the front of the chest and shoulder
  5. Hold for twenty to thirty seconds, then change sides
ea_side_chest_stretch_on_wall

  2. Extend your right arm straight over your head
  3. Slowly lower your right hand towards your left hand to stretch your back
  4. Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, feeling the stretch in your back and shoulders. Slowly return to the starting position and repeat on the other side by lying on your right side and following the same steps

Stretching - Mobility Revised

  2. Turn the palm to face backwards and away from your body
  3. Use the other hand to press gently down on that hand
  4. Keep the elbow straight and the shoulder pulled down

PurposeTurning the palm down changes which part of the biceps and forearm gets stretched, reaching fibres the thumb-down version misses. Worth doing both if the arm feels tight after heavy pulling.

  2. Keep the arm straight and at about shoulder height
  3. Press the palm into the wall and keep the shoulder down
  4. Rotate your torso away from the wall until you feel the stretch
  5. Hold for twenty seconds, then change arms

Stretching - Mobility Revised

PurposeThe wall lets you control the intensity precisely by turning your body, which makes it a strong choice for an arm that is genuinely tight. Also opens the front of that shoulder.

  2. Straighten that arm fully with the thumb pointing down
  3. Keep the shoulder pressed down away from your ear
  4. Turn your chest slowly away from the wall until the biceps stretches
  5. Hold for twenty to thirty seconds, then swap sides

Band Lying Press Down

Triceps

PurposeLying down pins your shoulder blades to the floor, so the shoulders cannot join in and the triceps has to straighten the arm on its own. The band pulls hardest at full extension, which is exactly where the triceps is strongest.

  1. Anchor the band to something solid behind your head and lie on your back
  2. Hold an end in each hand and bring your elbows up so the upper arms point at the ceiling
  3. Keep the upper arms still — only the forearms will move
  4. Straighten your elbows so your hands travel toward your hips and the band stretches
  5. Bend the elbows slowly to bring your hands back beside your ears

Band Skullcrusher

Triceps

PurposeLoads the triceps with the arms overhead, which stretches the long head — the part that runs to the shoulder blade and is missed by every pushdown. A band does this without the elbow pressure a bar puts on the joint in the same position.

  1. Anchor the band low behind you and lie on a bench or the floor with your head toward the anchor
  2. Hold both ends and press your arms straight up so the hands are over your shoulders
  3. Keep the upper arms vertical and locked in place
  4. Bend only the elbows to lower your hands toward your forehead
  5. Straighten the arms back to the start, stopping just short of locking the elbows
ea_band_skullcrusher

Band Triceps Pushdown Single Arm

Triceps

PurposeOne arm at a time, so a stronger triceps cannot cover for a weaker one — which matters because a lagging triceps is usually what stalls a bench press. A band makes this possible anywhere, without a cable stack.

  1. Anchor the band above head height and stand facing it, one step back
  2. Take the end in one hand with the elbow bent and tucked against your ribs
  3. Put the other hand on that elbow so you can feel it stay in place
  4. Push the hand down until the arm is straight, keeping the elbow pinned
  5. Let the band pull the hand back up slowly, then repeat and change arms

Cable Cross Pushdown

Triceps

PurposeCrossing the cables in front of you pulls each arm outward as well as up, so the triceps has to hold the arm in line as it straightens. That extra job hits the outer head, the one that gives the arm its shape just above the elbow.

  1. Set both pulleys at head height and take the left handle in your right hand and the right in your left
  2. Stand in the middle so the cables cross in front of your chest, elbows bent and at your sides
  3. Brace your stomach and lean forward very slightly from the hips
  4. Push both hands down and slightly outward until the arms are straight
  5. Return slowly to the bent position without letting the elbows drift forward

  2. Push up by extending both arms, keeping your knees on the floor. Lift your right hand off the floor, performing a rowing motion by bringing your elbow up towards the ceiling
  3. Return your right hand to the floor and lower your body to the starting position

Yoga Revised

  3. Press your feet back into your hands rather than pulling with your arms

  5. Breathe steadily and hold for fifteen to thirty seconds, then release slowly

Bridge Hip Abduction

  1. Begin by lying on your back with your knees bent, feet flat on the floor at shoulder width, and arms extended by your sides
  2. Lift your hips off the floor to form a straight line from your shoulders to your knees, engaging your glutes and core

  4. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions

Purposenot written yet (H3 pending)

  1. Lie down on your back with your knees bent, feet together on the floor, and arms resting at your sides

  4. Return to the initial position and repeat

Bridge with Alternating Leg Raise

Yoga No purpose

Purposenot written yet (H3 pending)

  1. Begin by lying on your back with your knees bent, feet flat on the floor, and arms resting by your sides
  2. Lift your hips off the floor to form a straight line from your shoulders to your knees, engaging your glutes and core
  3. While keeping your hips elevated, extend your right leg straight keeping it in level with torso, then lower it back to the starting position
  4. Repeat the movement with your left leg, extending it straight keeping it in level with torso, then lowering it back to the starting position. Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions

Butterfly Yoga Pose

Yoga No purpose

Purposenot written yet (H3 pending)

  1. Sit on the floor with your legs bent and the soles of your feet pressed together, allowing your knees to fall out to the sides
  2. Hold your feet with both hands and sit up tall, then lean forward slightly towards the floor, creating a gentle arch in your back

Cat Pose

Yoga Revised

PurposeRounding the spine on all fours moves the vertebrae through a range that a day of sitting rarely uses, which can help ease stiffness. Paired with its opposite, it is the standard way to warm the back up before anything else.

  1. Start on hands and knees with wrists under shoulders and knees under hips
  2. Keep the spine long and neutral to begin
  3. Breathe out and round your back toward the ceiling, one segment at a time
  4. Let your head drop and draw your stomach up toward your spine
  5. Hold for a breath, then return to neutral or move into the opposite arch
ea_cat_pose

Cat Stretch

Yoga No purpose

Purposenot written yet (H3 pending)

  1. Begin on your hands and knees in a tabletop position, with your wrists aligned under your shoulders and your knees aligned under your hips
  2. Inhale deeply, then slowly arch your back upwards towards the ceiling, tucking your chin towards your chest and drawing your navel in towards your spine
  3. Hold the arched position for a few seconds, feeling the stretch along your spine and back muscles
  4. Exhale and slowly return to the starting tabletop position. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions
ea_cat_stretch lower_back

Chair Pose

Yoga

PurposeHolds a squat position with the arms overhead, which works the legs and asks the shoulders and upper back to stay open under load. Simple, and it burns much sooner than it looks like it should.

  1. Stand with your feet together or hip width apart
  2. Bend your knees and sit your hips back as if lowering into a chair
  3. Keep your weight in your heels and your chest lifted
  4. Raise both arms overhead alongside your ears, palms facing each other
  5. Hold for thirty seconds, breathing steadily, then stand up slowly
ea_chair_pose

Child Pose Arms Extended Left Right

Yoga

PurposeWalking the hands to one side turns the rest position into a side stretch, reaching the lats and the space between the ribs. A way to get two things from one shape while you catch your breath.

  1. Kneel with your big toes together and your knees wide apart
  2. Sit your hips back toward your heels and lower your chest to the floor
  3. Walk both hands across to one side, keeping the hips centred
  4. Feel the stretch down the opposite side of your ribs and back
  5. Hold for thirty seconds, then walk the hands across to the other side
ea_child_pose_arms_extended_left_right

Child Pose Arms on Side

Yoga

PurposeThe most restful version, with the arms back and the shoulders completely released. Used to slow the breathing down between hard efforts, or at the end of a session to finish calm.

  1. Kneel and sit your hips back onto your heels
  2. Bring your knees together or slightly apart, whichever is comfortable
  3. Fold forward and rest your forehead on the mat
  4. Lay your arms back alongside your body with the palms facing up
  5. Let the shoulders drop and breathe slowly for thirty seconds or more
ea_child_pose_arms_on_side

Child Pose Elbows on Block

Yoga

PurposeRaising the elbows on a block deepens the shoulder stretch, which turns a rest pose into targeted work for overhead range. Useful for anyone whose arms will not go straight up beside the ears.

  1. Kneel with your knees wide and sit your hips back toward your heels
  2. Place a block in front of you and rest both elbows on it
  3. Bring your palms together behind your head
  4. Let your chest sink toward the floor between your arms
  5. Hold for thirty seconds, breathing into the shoulders and upper back
ea_child_pose_elbows_on_block

Child Pose Up

Yoga No purpose

Purposenot written yet (H3 pending)

  1. Begin by kneeling on the floor with your knees together or slightly apart, and your big toes touching
  2. Sit back on your heels, extending your arms forward on the floor, lowering your torso down between your thighs
  3. Rest your forehead on the floor, keeping your arms extended out in front of you with palms facing down
  4. Hold this position for the desired duration, breathing deeply and allowing your body to relax into the stretch
ea_child_pose_up lower_back

Cobra Full Push Up

Yoga No purpose

Purposenot written yet (H3 pending)

  1. Begin in a plank position with your hands placed under your shoulders, your body forming a straight line from head to heels
  2. Perform a push-up by lowering your body towards the floor by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your sides
  3. As your chest reaches the floor, leave your hips on the floor and press through your palms to lift your chest up, straightening your arms and arching your back into the cobra position
  4. Bend your arms to lower your chest back to the floor, then press through your palms to lift your body back to the starting plank position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions

Cobra Push Up

Yoga No purpose Revised

Purposenot written yet (H3 pending)

  1. Begin by lying face down on the floor with your legs extended straight behind you and your hands placed at shoulder level, palms flat on the floor and elbows close to your sides
  2. Engage your core and press through your palms to lift your chest off the floor, straightening your arms to come into the cobra position
  3. Keep your hips on the floor. Hold the cobra position for a second, feeling the stretch in your lower back and abdomen
  4. Slowly lower your chest back to the floor by bending your elbows, returning to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions
ea_cobra_push_up elbowlower_backshoulderupper_backwrist

Cobra Side Ab Stretch

Yoga No purpose

Purposenot written yet (H3 pending)

  1. Begin by lying face down on the floor with your legs extended straight behind you and your hands placed at shoulder level, palms flat on the floor
  2. Press through your palms to lift your chest off the floor, straightening your arms to come into the cobra position, keeping your hips on the floor
  3. From the cobra position, slowly rotate your torso to the right, looking over your right shoulder, and hold the stretch for a moment, feeling the stretch along the left side of your abdomen. Return to the center cobra position
  4. Slowly rotate your torso to the left, looking over your left shoulder, and hold the stretch, feeling the stretch along the right side of your abdomen. Return to the center cobra position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions
ea_cobra_side_ab_stretch lower_backupper_back

Cobra Yoga Pose Hold

Yoga No purpose

Purposenot written yet (H3 pending)

  1. Begin by lying face down on the floor with your legs extended straight behind you and your hands placed at shoulder level, palms flat on the floor
  2. Engage your core and press through your palms to lift your chest off the floor, straightening your arms to come into the cobra position, keeping your hips on the floor
  3. Hold the cobra position, keeping your arms straight and your chest lifted, while breathing steadily
ea_cobra_yoga_pose_hold lower_backupper_back

Crab Pose

Yoga No purpose

Purposenot written yet (H3 pending)

  1. Begin by sitting on the floor with your legs bent, feet flat on the floor, and hands placed behind you with your fingers pointing towards your body
  2. Engage your core and press through your palms and feet to lift your hips off the floor, creating a tabletop position with your body
  3. Hold this position, ensuring your hips are lifted high and your torso is parallel to the floor, while keeping your head in line with your spine
  4. After holding the position for the desired duration, slowly lower your hips back to the floor and return to the starting position
ea_crab_pose wrist

Crescent Moon Pose

Yoga Revised

PurposeA lunge with the arms overhead that stretches the front of the back hip while the front leg works to hold you up. It opens the hip and challenges balance in the same shape.

  1. Step one foot well forward into a lunge with the back heel lifted
  2. Bend the front knee to about ninety degrees over the ankle, adjusting to what feels comfortable and controlled
  3. Squeeze the back glute to push that hip forward
  4. Raise both arms overhead and lengthen upward through your fingers
  5. Hold for thirty seconds, breathing steadily, then change legs
ea_crescent_moon_pose

Criss Cross Bow Tie Pose

Yoga

PurposeCrossing the arms behind the back opens both shoulders in a direction almost nothing else reaches. It targets exactly the tightness that comes from spending the day with the arms in front of you.

  1. Lie face down or kneel tall with your shoulders relaxed
  2. Reach both arms behind your back and cross them at the forearms
  3. Take hold of the opposite upper arm or elbow if you can reach
  4. Draw the shoulder blades together and let the chest open
  5. Hold for twenty to thirty seconds, then switch which arm is on top
ea_criss_cross_bow_tie_pose

Crow Pose

Yoga Revised

PurposeThe first arm balance most people learn, and it builds real wrist, shoulder and stomach strength. Almost everyone falls forward the first several times — put a cushion in front of you and expect it.

  1. Squat down with your feet together and place your hands flat on the floor, shoulder width apart
  2. Bend your elbows slightly and rest your knees high on the backs of your upper arms
  3. Shift your weight forward onto your hands and look slightly ahead, not down
  4. Lift one foot, then the other, until only your hands touch the floor
  5. Hold for as long as you can control, then step the feet back down — ease off right away if you feel wrist pain
ea_crow_pose

Double Pigeon Pose

Yoga

PurposeStacking the shins stretches the outside of both hips at once, which is where tightness settles in anyone who sits. Intense — sit on a cushion if the knees are far off the floor.

  1. Sit on the floor and bend one leg so the shin is parallel to the front of the mat
  2. Stack the other shin directly on top, ankle over knee and knee over ankle
  3. Sit up tall on both sitting bones
  4. Stay upright or fold slowly forward from the hips
  5. Hold for a minute, breathing into the outer hips, then swap which leg is on top
ea_double_pigeon_pose hip

Downward Dog Toe to Heel

Yoga

PurposePedalling the heels one at a time stretches each calf and hamstring separately, which is more effective than holding both still. It is also how you find out which side is tighter.

  1. Start on hands and knees, then lift the hips up and back into an inverted V
  2. Press the floor away with your hands and lengthen your spine
  3. Bend one knee and press the opposite heel toward the floor
  4. Hold for a breath, then switch, pedalling slowly between sides
  5. Continue for thirty to sixty seconds
ea_downward_dog_toe_to_heel wrist

Downward Dog with Fingers Facing Feet

Yoga

PurposeTurning the fingers backwards puts the stretch into the underside of the forearms and the wrists, which is exactly what needs to open before push-ups, front squats or handstands. Go gently.

  1. Start on hands and knees and turn both hands so the fingers point toward your feet
  2. Press the palms flat and keep the elbows soft
  3. Lift your hips up and back into a downward dog shape
  4. Take only as much weight into the hands as the wrists comfortably allow
  5. Hold for fifteen to twenty seconds, then come down and shake the wrists out
ea_downward_dog_with_fingers_facing_feet wrist

Dumbbell Single Leg Glute Bridge

Yoga No purpose

Purposenot written yet (H3 pending)

  1. Begin by lying flat on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor. Hold a dumbbell across your hips with both hands. Extend your left leg straight out in front of you, keeping it in line with your right thigh
  2. Engage your core and squeeze your glutes. Drive through your right heel to lift your hips towards the ceiling, forming a straight line from your shoulders to your right knee
  3. Hold the top position briefly, squeezing your glutes and maintaining a straight line with your body
  4. Lower your hips back to the starting position with control, ensuring your left leg remains extended. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other leg
ea_dumbbell_single_leg_glute_bridge hip

Eagle Arms Chin Into Chest

Yoga

PurposeWrapping the arms spreads the shoulder blades apart, stretching the upper back where a desk day makes it stiff. Adding the chin tuck reaches the back of the neck at the same time.

  1. Sit or stand tall and extend both arms straight in front of you
  2. Cross one arm over the other at the elbows and wrap the forearms if you can
  3. Lift the elbows to shoulder height and push the hands forward
  4. Tuck your chin toward your chest and round the upper back slightly
  5. Hold for twenty to thirty seconds, then unwrap and cross the other arm on top
ea_eagle_arms_chin_into_chest

Easy Pose Neck Stretch

Yoga

PurposeReleases the sides of the neck, which carry tension from screens and from stress. Using the hand adds only a little weight — the neck needs far less force than any other area.

  1. Sit cross-legged with your spine tall and shoulders relaxed
  2. Let one hand rest on the floor beside you and press it down gently
  3. Tilt your head so the opposite ear moves toward that shoulder
  4. Rest the free hand lightly on the side of your head — do not pull
  5. Hold for twenty to thirty seconds, then change sides
ea_easy_pose_neck_stretch neck

Easy Seated Twist Pose

Yoga Revised

PurposeHelps maintain rotation in the spine, a movement that's often among the first the back loses and misses most. Done sitting, so it can be fitted into a working day without a mat.

  1. Sit cross-legged with both sitting bones evenly on the floor
  2. Lengthen your spine upward before you turn
  3. Place one hand behind you and the other on the opposite knee
  4. Turn your ribs, then your shoulders, then finally your head to that side
  5. Hold for thirty seconds, breathing, then unwind and twist the other way
ea_easy_seated_twist_pose wrist

Extended Side Angle

Yoga No purpose

Purposenot written yet (H3 pending)

  1. Stand with your feet wide apart, about 3-4 feet, with your right foot turned out 90 degrees and your left foot slightly turned in. Place your hands on your hips
  2. Bend your right knee, ensuring it aligns over your right ankle, and lower your right thigh until it is parallel to the floor. Extend your left leg straight
  3. Lean to your right side by bending your right knee further and place your right elbow on your right thigh. Raise your left arm overhead, creating a straight line from your left hand to your left foot
  4. Hold the position for a moment, then return to the starting position with control. Repeat on the other side
ea_extended_side_angle lower_back

Extended Side Angle Pose

Yoga

PurposeWorks the legs while stretching the whole side of the body from the back foot to the top hand. It combines strength and length in one shape, which is why it appears in almost every sequence.

  1. Step your feet wide apart and turn the front foot out ninety degrees
  2. Bend the front knee over the ankle and keep the back leg straight
  3. Rest the front forearm on the front thigh or take the hand to the floor
  4. Reach the top arm over your ear so it makes a line with the back leg
  5. Hold for thirty seconds, breathing into the top ribs, then change sides
ea_extended_side_angle_pose

Extended Side Angle Pose with Block

Yoga

PurposeThe block raises the floor to meet your hand, so you can hold the full shape without collapsing the chest toward the thigh. The version to use until the hips open enough for the floor.

  1. Step wide and turn the front foot out, placing a block beside the front ankle
  2. Bend the front knee over the ankle with the back leg straight
  3. Rest the front hand on the block instead of the floor
  4. Open the chest toward the ceiling and reach the top arm over your ear
  5. Hold for thirty seconds, then change sides
ea_extended_side_angle_pose_with_block

Gate Pose Rounding Spine Looking Up

Yoga Revised

PurposeA side bend from a kneeling position that opens the ribs and the side of the waist, plus the inner thigh of the extended leg. It reaches the breathing muscles between the ribs more directly than most stretches do.

  1. Kneel on one knee and extend the other leg straight out to the side, foot flat
  2. Rest the same-side hand lightly on the extended leg
  3. Reach the opposite arm up and over toward the extended foot
  4. Turn your chest slightly upward and lengthen through the top ribs
  5. Hold for thirty seconds, breathing wide, then change sides
ea_gate_pose_rounding_spine_looking_up

Gate Pose Variation Arm Extended on Side

Yoga Revised

PurposeA gentler gate pose where the arm reaches along the leg rather than overhead, which keeps the shoulder out of it. A useful option when you want less overhead shoulder demand while still opening the side body.

  1. Kneel on one knee with the other leg extended straight to the side
  2. Keep the extended foot flat and the hips facing forward
  3. Slide the same-side hand down along the extended leg
  4. Let the opposite arm rest on your hip or reach softly overhead
  5. Hold for thirty seconds, then swap legs
ea_gate_pose_variation_arm_extended_on_side

Half Lotus

Yoga

PurposeA seated position that opens the outside of one hip at a time and is comfortable enough to hold for a long while. Used for sitting and breathing work rather than as a stretch to push into.

  1. Sit on the floor with both legs straight out in front of you
  2. Bend one knee and place that foot on the opposite thigh, sole facing up
  3. Tuck the other foot under the opposite thigh
  4. Sit tall on both sitting bones with the hands resting on the knees
  5. Hold and breathe for a minute or more, then change which leg is on top
ea_half_lotus

Half Monkey Pose

Yoga Revised

PurposeA hamstring stretch approached from a kneeling lunge, which lets you control the depth precisely with your hips. It is a safer route toward the full splits, and useful on its own.

  1. Start in a low lunge with one foot forward and the back knee on the mat
  2. Slide the front foot forward and straighten that leg, toes pointing up
  3. Sit your hips back over the back knee
  4. Keep your back long and hinge forward from the hips, not the spine
  5. Hold for thirty seconds, then change legs
ea_half_monkey_pose

Happy Baby

Yoga Revised

PurposeOpens the inner thighs and the lower back at the same time, in a position where the floor supports the whole spine. A well-supported hip stretch. Ease off or stop if you feel sharp or increasing back pain.

  1. Lie on your back and draw both knees toward your armpits
  2. Reach up and hold the outside edges of your feet, or your shins
  3. Keep the soles of the feet facing the ceiling and the shins vertical
  4. Press the feet up into your hands and let your lower back settle onto the floor
  5. Hold for thirty seconds or longer, rocking gently if it feels good
ea_happy_baby hip

High Plank

Yoga No purpose

Purposenot written yet (H3 pending)

  1. Begin on the floor on your hands and knees. Position your hands directly under your shoulders and your knees under your hips
  2. Extend your legs straight back, one at a time, coming onto the balls of your feet to form a straight line from your head to your heels. Your body should be in a high plank position
  3. Engage your core, glutes, and legs to maintain a straight body line. Keep your shoulders directly over your wrists
  4. Hold the plank position for the desired amount of time, maintaining proper form and steady breathing
ea_high_plank elbowwrist

Lord of the Dance

Yoga

PurposeCombines a standing balance with a deep stretch through the front of the thigh, hip and chest. Demanding on all three at once, which is what makes it a good test of how the whole front line is moving.

  1. Stand tall and shift your weight onto one foot
  2. Bend the other knee and take hold of that ankle or foot from the inside
  3. Press the lifted foot back into your hand as you hinge forward slightly
  4. Reach the opposite arm forward for balance and open your chest
  5. Hold for fifteen to thirty seconds, then come down and change sides
ea_lord_of_the_dance

Modified Hindu Push Up

Yoga No purpose

Purposenot written yet (H3 pending)

  1. Begin in a plank position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and your feet hip-width apart. Your body should form a straight line from head to heels
  2. Lower your chest towards the floor by bending your elbows, keeping your body straight
  3. Push through your hands to raise your hips up and back into a downward-facing dog position, forming an inverted V-shape with your body
  4. Lower your hips and return to the plank position by moving your body forward. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions
ea_modified_hindu_push_up elbowshoulderwrist

Monkey Pose

Yoga Revised

PurposeThe full front splits, which asks for length in the hamstring of one leg and the front of the hip of the other at the same time. It takes months of consistent work — use blocks and go slowly.

  1. Start in a low lunge with blocks placed either side of your hips
  2. Straighten the front leg and slide the heel forward, toes pointing up
  3. Slide the back knee backwards, keeping the hips square to the front
  4. Take your weight on the blocks and lower only as far as is comfortable
  5. Hold for thirty seconds, breathing, then come out carefully and change sides
ea_monkey_pose

One Arm Cow Face Pose - Easy

Yoga

PurposeStretches the back of one shoulder and the triceps at the same time, in the overhead position that most people cannot reach comfortably. Working one arm shows plainly which side is tighter.

  1. Sit or stand tall with your shoulders relaxed
  2. Raise one arm overhead and bend the elbow so the hand drops behind your head
  3. Use the other hand to hold that elbow gently
  4. Draw the elbow slightly back and toward the midline without arching your back
  5. Hold for twenty to thirty seconds, then change arms
ea_one_arm_cow_face_pose_easy

Pigeon Glutes Stretch

Yoga Revised

PurposeA deep stretch for the back of the hip, including the muscles that sit deep beneath the glutes. Expect a strong stretch, not pain — ease off if it turns sharp, or if you feel radiating pain, numbness or tingling down the leg.

  1. From hands and knees, bring one knee forward behind the same-side wrist
  2. Angle the shin across your body and slide the other leg straight back
  3. Square your hips toward the floor, using a cushion under the front hip if needed
  4. Stay upright or fold forward over the front leg
  5. Hold for a minute, breathing slowly, then change sides
ea_pigeon_glutes_stretch hip

Pigeon Pose

Yoga

PurposeOpens the back of the front hip and the front of the back hip at the same time — the two areas that between them decide how freely you walk and run. One of the most useful shapes in yoga for anyone who trains.

  1. From all fours, slide one knee forward toward the same-side hand
  2. Let the shin angle across the mat and extend the other leg straight back
  3. Keep the back leg's toes pointing straight down and the hips level
  4. Walk your hands forward and lower your chest toward the floor
  5. Hold for a minute, then press back up and change sides
ea_pigeon_pose hip

Puppy Pose

Yoga

PurposeStretches the shoulders and the upper back with the hips staying high, so the lower back is not involved. The best shape for opening overhead range if the lower back does not tolerate a deep fold.

  1. Start on hands and knees with the hips directly over the knees
  2. Walk your hands forward and lower your chest toward the floor
  3. Keep the hips stacked over the knees — do not sit back toward the heels
  4. Rest your forehead or chin on the mat and let the chest sink
  5. Hold for thirty to sixty seconds, breathing into the upper back
ea_puppy_pose

Pyramid Pose - Parsvottanasana

Yoga

PurposeA standing hamstring stretch with the hips square, which stops the pelvis from twisting to make the stretch easier. That squareness is what makes it more effective than reaching for one toe.

  1. Step one foot forward about a leg's length, both legs straight
  2. Turn the back foot out slightly and square both hips to the front
  3. Lengthen your spine, then hinge forward over the front leg from the hips
  4. Rest your hands on the floor, your shin, or blocks
  5. Hold for thirty seconds, then rise slowly and change sides
ea_pyramid_pose_parsvottanasana

Pyramid Pose Blocks

Yoga Revised

PurposeBlocks under the hands bring the floor up to you, so the back can stay neutral instead of rounding to reach. Keeping the spine neutral is what lets the stretch reach the hamstrings instead of the lower back, so this is the better version for most people.

  1. Place a block on each side of your front foot
  2. Step the other foot back a leg's length and square your hips forward
  3. Keep both legs straight and lengthen through the spine
  4. Hinge from the hips and rest your hands on the blocks
  5. Hold for thirty seconds with a neutral spine, then change sides
ea_pyramid_pose_blocks

Pyramid Pose Calf Blocks

Yoga

PurposeRaising the front toes on a block adds a calf stretch on top of the hamstring one, so the whole back of the leg lengthens together. Useful for anyone whose ankles limit their squat.

  1. Place a block under the ball of the front foot so the toes are raised
  2. Step the back foot away a leg's length with both legs straight
  3. Square your hips and lengthen your spine
  4. Hinge forward from the hips over the front leg
  5. Hold for thirty seconds, feeling the calf and hamstring together, then swap
ea_pyramid_pose_calf_blocks ankle

Pyramid Prayer

Yoga

PurposeAdding the prayer hands behind the back turns a hamstring stretch into a shoulder and wrist opener as well. Two very different tight areas addressed in one shape, which is efficient if time is short.

  1. Bring your palms together behind your back with the fingers pointing up
  2. Step one foot forward a leg's length and square your hips
  3. Keep both legs straight and lengthen your spine
  4. Hinge forward over the front leg, keeping the palms pressed together
  5. Hold for twenty to thirty seconds, then rise and change sides
ea_pyramid_prayer

Reclining Pigeon Pose

Yoga Revised

PurposeThe same hip stretch as pigeon but lying down, where the floor supports your spine and you control the pressure with your hands. Often kinder to the knees, and a useful option to try if your back feels stiff -- ease in gently and stop if anything feels wrong.

  1. Lie on your back with both knees bent and feet on the floor
  2. Cross one ankle over the opposite thigh, just above the knee
  3. Thread one hand through the gap and clasp the back of the supporting thigh
  4. Draw that leg toward your chest, letting the crossed knee open outward
  5. Hold for a minute, keeping your head on the floor, then change sides
ea_reclining_pigeon_pose hip

Resistance Band Glute Bridge

Yoga No purpose

Purposenot written yet (H3 pending)

  1. Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart. Place a loop resistance band just above your knees. Keep your hands extended by your sides with hands firm on the floor
  2. Engage your core and glutes, and lift your hips towards the ceiling, forming a straight line from your shoulders to your knees
  3. Hold the bridge position for a moment, squeezing your glutes at the top
  4. Slowly lower your hips back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions
ea_resistance_band_glute_bridge hip

Resistance Band Glute Bridge Abduction

Yoga No purpose Revised

Purposenot written yet (H3 pending)

  1. Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart. Place a loop resistance band just above your knees. Keep your hands extended by your sides with hands firm on the floor
  2. Engage your core and glutes, and lift your hips towards the ceiling, forming a straight line from your shoulders to your knees
  3. While holding the bridge position, press your knees outward against the resistance band to stretch them as far as you can control
  4. Slowly bring your knees back together, then lower your hips back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions

Restful Cow Face Pose Legs

Yoga

PurposeStacking the knees stretches the outside of both hips at once and can be held for several minutes without effort. A position to settle into at the end of a session rather than to work at.

  1. Sit on the floor and bend one knee, drawing the foot toward the opposite hip
  2. Stack the other knee directly on top and bring that foot to the other hip
  3. Sit on a cushion if your knees are high or your back rounds
  4. Rest your hands on the top knee and sit tall
  5. Hold for one to three minutes, then swap which knee is on top

Reverse Prayer

Yoga

PurposePressing the palms together behind the back demands more from the shoulders and wrists than almost any other stretch. If it is not accessible, holding opposite elbows behind the back does the same job more gently.

  1. Stand or sit tall with your shoulders rolled back and down
  2. Bring both hands behind your back with the fingers pointing down
  3. Rotate the hands until the fingers point up and the palms meet
  4. Press the palms together and draw the elbows back to open the chest
  5. Hold for twenty to thirty seconds, breathing steadily
ea_reverse_prayer

Revolved Side Angle Pose with Prayer Hands

Yoga

PurposeCombines a lunge with a deep twist, so the legs work while the spine rotates against the resistance of the thigh. It reaches rotation range that a seated twist cannot, because the hips are locked by the stance.

  1. Step into a lunge with the back heel lifted and the front knee over the ankle
  2. Bring your palms together in front of your chest
  3. Turn your torso toward the front leg and hook the opposite elbow outside that knee
  4. Press the elbow and knee against each other to deepen the turn
  5. Hold for thirty seconds, breathing, then unwind and change sides
ea_revolved_side_angle_pose_with_prayer_hands

Revolved Side Angle Pose with Prayer Hands Beginner

Yoga

PurposeThe same twist with the back knee down, which removes the balance demand so you can concentrate on the rotation itself. This is where to start before attempting the full version.

  1. Kneel on one knee with the other foot forward, both bent to ninety degrees
  2. Bring your palms together at your chest and sit tall
  3. Turn your ribs toward the front leg
  4. Rest the opposite elbow on the outside of the front knee and press gently
  5. Hold for thirty seconds, then unwind and swap sides
ea_revolved_side_angle_pose_with_prayer_hands_beginner

Runners Lunge

Yoga

PurposeOpens the front of the back hip and the inside of the front one, which is the pair that limits stride length in running. Ninety seconds of this before a run changes how the first kilometre feels.

  1. From all fours, step one foot forward to the outside of the same-side hand
  2. Straighten the back leg and press through the heel or rest the knee down
  3. Lower onto your forearms or keep the hands flat, whichever you can hold
  4. Let the front hip sink toward the floor and keep the chest open
  5. Hold for thirty to sixty seconds, then change sides

  2. Without bending your elbows, squeeze your shoulder blades together, allowing your chest to lower slightly towards the floor

Scorpion Twist Pose

Yoga

PurposeA face-down twist that stretches the front of the shoulder and chest on one side while opening the hip on the other. It reaches two very different tight areas in a single position, without any strength demand.

  1. Lie face down with both arms out wide at shoulder height, palms down
  2. Bend one knee and lift that leg
  3. Reach it across your body toward the opposite hand, letting the hip roll
  4. Keep both shoulders pressing toward the floor as the leg crosses
  5. Hold for thirty seconds, breathing, then unwind slowly and change sides

Side Lying Parsva Savasana Variation

Yoga

PurposeA resting position on the side that requires nothing from you at all, used to finish a session or to calm the breathing down. Rest is part of training, not the absence of it.

  1. Lie on one side with your knees bent and stacked
  2. Rest your head on your lower arm or a cushion
  3. Place the top arm wherever it is comfortable — in front of you or along your side
  4. Let your whole body soften and stop holding any position
  5. Breathe slowly for one to five minutes, then roll up carefully

Wild Thing Pose

Yoga Revised

PurposeA large chest and shoulder opener done from a side plank, which also asks the glutes to hold the hips high. It is the most extended front-body position in common practice — go into it warm, never cold.

  1. Start in a side plank on one hand with the feet stacked
  2. Step the top foot back behind you and place it flat on the floor
  3. Press through both feet and lift your hips high
  4. Sweep the top arm overhead and let your chest open toward the ceiling
  5. Hold for fifteen to twenty seconds, then come down carefully and change sides

Yoga Flow Sequences Sun Salutations

Yoga Revised

PurposeA sequence rather than a single pose: it moves the whole spine through flexion and extension while warming the shoulders, hips and hamstrings. The most efficient general warm-up there is when you have five minutes and no equipment.

  1. Stand tall, then reach both arms overhead on an inhale
  2. Fold forward over your legs, then lift halfway with a neutral spine
  3. Step or jump back to a plank, lower down, and lift the chest into a gentle backbend
  4. Push the hips up and back into a downward dog and hold for a breath
  5. Step the feet back to the hands, fold, and rise to standing — then repeat the round
